name: Research Protocol Readiness
promise: Turn one research question into a falsifiable protocol ready for the qualified review it actually needs.
summary: A locked question, evidence map, protocol and analysis plan, only applicable ethics or data modules, and an honest ready-for-qualified-review, repair-required, or no-go receipt.
useWhen: A defined question needs a reproducible protocol before data collection.
A bench, computational, observational, or participant study needs its assumptions and analysis challenged.
notFor: Executing a study or recruiting participants.
Automatically treating every study as a clinical or regulated human-subject investigation.
Making efficacy, safety, diagnostic, or regulatory claims.

skills.name: Customer Research
skills.role: Participant context, burden, comprehension, recruitment assumptions, consent language, withdrawals, and qualitative evidence boundaries

skills.name: Analytics
skills.role: Research question structure, endpoint definitions, sample-size rationale, analysis plan, missing data, reproducibility, and reporting integrity

skills.name: Product Marketing
skills.role: Separation of research rationale, product facts, proposed outcomes, public language, and prohibited efficacy claims

skills.name: Documentation Writer
skills.role: Auditable protocol, investigator, participant, ethics, registration, and publication packages

skills.name: Security Review
skills.role: Privacy, access, retention, de-identification, audit, export, deletion, incident, and sensitive-data boundaries

workstreams.name: Question and evidence map
workstreams.brief: Lock the question, prior evidence, hypotheses, variables, endpoints, exclusions, and claim boundary.

workstreams.name: Protocol and analysis
workstreams.brief: Create the reproducible protocol and analysis plan plus only applicable participant, data, regulatory, or operational modules.

workstreams.name: Qualified-path review
workstreams.brief: Challenge bias, feasibility, consent, privacy, analysis flexibility, and the exact qualified review still required.

outputs: Locked research question and evidence map
guardrails: Do not recruit, consent, intervene, collect data, access records, or register a study without separate approval and applicable qualified authorization.
Do not invent ethics, legal, clinical, statistical, or regulatory approval.
Do not add participant or health-data ceremony to a bench or computational protocol without activation evidence.
Minimize sensitive data and preserve withdrawal, deletion, access, retention, and incident boundaries when applicable.
Ready-for-qualified-review means the package is coherent enough for the applicable expert or authority to review; it does not approve or execute the study.
verification: Trace the research question and design choices to evidence.
Challenge confounding, bias, missingness, multiplicity, power, and analysis flexibility as applicable.
Dry-run the protocol with synthetic or non-sensitive fixtures where legitimate.
State the exact qualified review required before execution and every claim the protocol cannot establish.
Lock one falsifiable question and the claims the study could and could not support.
Write the minimum reproducible protocol and prespecified analysis plan.
Activate ethics, privacy, regulatory, and operational modules only from the actual design.
Use independent challenge to identify the exact qualified approval still required before execution.

expectations.statement: The research question, hypothesis, variables, and endpoint are falsifiable.
The protocol can be followed without unstated material decisions.
The analysis plan defines outcomes, exclusions, missingness, uncertainty, and reporting.
Participant recruitment, consent, burden, withdrawal, and adverse-event boundaries are explicit. Applicable when: Living people are recruited, observed, surveyed, tested, or intervened upon.
Sensitive health-data collection and handling are minimized and controlled. Applicable when: Health, biometric, diagnostic, treatment, or similarly sensitive data are used.
Additional protections for the named vulnerable population are explicit. Applicable when: The population has reduced autonomy or additional vulnerability.
Applicable regulated-product and claim boundaries are mapped for qualified review. Applicable when: The protocol involves a regulated product, indication, diagnostic, or efficacy claim.
Site consistency, delegation, versioning, and data reconciliation are controlled. Applicable when: More than one site, investigator, or operational unit executes the protocol.
Remote identity, environment, support, and failure handling are bounded. Applicable when: Material procedures or measurements occur outside a controlled study site.
Specimen collection, custody, storage, disposal, and biosafety paths are explicit. Applicable when: Biological specimens are collected, stored, transported, analyzed, or disposed.

Research protocol readiness produces enough evidence for an independent readiness decision. The possible decisions are ready-for-qualified-review, repair-required, no-go. Ready-for-qualified-review means the package is coherent enough for the applicable expert or authority to review; it does not approve or execute the study.
failureModes: missing evidence for the declared outcome
decision made from assumptions or unverified claims
